tools.name: get_chat_conversation_events
tools.description: Retrieves the events of a specific Chat conversation, newest first, with pagination support: messages, key changes, group changes, and read receipts. Events with an id above the conversation's last_read_event_id are unread: they come after the point you read up to. To collect them, page until an event's id is at or below it. Only `id` and `encoded_event` are always present. Events are either end-to-end encrypted or unencrypted, such as messages sent before the conversation was encrypted. Encrypted events carry `conversation_key_version`, and usually `conversation_token` and `message_event_signature`; treat an encrypted event without `message_event_signature` as unverified. An event without `conversation_key_version` is unencrypted. Decode each `encoded_event` client-side, and decrypt it with the conversation key named by `conversation_key_version` when that is present. A page holds up to `max_results` events and can hold fewer while `has_more` is true. For 1:1 conversations, provide the recipient's user ID; the server constructs the canonical conversation ID from the authenticated user and recipient.

chat_message_event.fields.description: A comma separated list of ChatMessageEvent fields to display.

max_results.description: The maximum number of events to return.

pagination_token.description: The next_token from a previous response, to fetch the next page.

tools.name: get_chat_conversations
tools.description:
Retrieves a list of Chat conversations for the authenticated user's inbox, newest first: the most recently active conversation comes first. The unread, last_read_event_id and newest_event_id fields give your read state, computed from your latest read receipt and each conversation's latest notifying message. Request them with chat_conversation.fields=unread,last_read_event_id,newest_event_id.

The filters unread_only, type, is_archived, is_muted, participant_ids, participant_query, start_time and end_time are optional, and all filters must match (AND). participant_query keeps conversations where another participant's username, or a word of their display name, starts with the query, ignoring case and accents; with a leading @ it matches usernames only. It considers the 100 people who best match the query, uses only public profile information, and never matches group names, nicknames or messages. start_time and end_time apply to the time of each conversation's latest message.

Each page covers max_results conversations and returns those that match, so a page can hold fewer than max_results, or none, while meta.next_token is set and has_more is true: keep paging, passing meta.next_token as pagination_token. Once a page reaches a conversation whose latest message is older than start_time, has_more is false. A pagination_token only works with the same filters as the request that returned it; with other filters, the request fails with a 400.

When both are provided, `start_time` must be earlier than `end_time`.

chat_conversation.fields.description: A comma separated list of ChatConversation fields to display.

end_time.description: ISO 8601, e.g. 2026-10-17T00:00:00Z. Chats whose latest message is before this time.

expansions.description: A comma separated list of fields to expand.

is_archived.description: true: only archived; false: only not archived. Omit for both.

is_muted.description: true: only muted; false: only not muted. Omit for both.

max_results.description: Conversations covered per page (1-1000, default 200). Filtered pages can return fewer.

pagination_token.description: meta.next_token from the previous page. Send the same filters with it, or the request fails.

participant_ids.description: Comma-separated numeric user IDs (1-10), all in the chat. Names or @handles: use participant_query.

participant_query.description: Name or @username prefix (1-50 chars); keeps chats where any other participant matches it.

start_time.description: ISO 8601, e.g. 2026-10-16T00:00:00Z. Chats whose latest message is at or after this time.

type.description: Only direct (1:1) or only group conversations. Omit for both.

unread_only.description: Return only unread conversations. A page can be short; keep paging while has_more.

user.fields.description: A comma separated list of User fields to display.

tools.name: send_chat_message
tools.description: Sends a message or reaction to a specific Chat conversation. Send `encoded_message_create_event`, an end-to-end encrypted event built with the Chat XDK. `content`, a plaintext message or reaction sent unencrypted, is only a fallback for a 1:1 conversation that X Chat can't encrypt because one of the two users has connected an enterprise app that reads their DMs; check that the recipient's `receives_your_chat` user field is `unencrypted` before using it. Otherwise a `content` send is refused, and retrying it won't help: HTTP 400 https://api.x.com/2/problems/encryption-required when the conversation can be encrypted or is a group (send `encoded_message_create_event` instead), 400 https://api.x.com/2/problems/xchat-setup-required when you haven't set up X Chat, 400 https://api.x.com/2/problems/recipient-xchat-setup-required when the recipient hasn't, and 403 https://api.x.com/2/problems/message-request-not-supported when it would be a message request. HTTP 503 https://api.x.com/2/problems/chat-permissions-unavailable means the check failed and nothing was sent; retry it. For 1:1 conversations, provide the recipient's user ID; the server constructs the canonical conversation ID from the authenticated user and recipient. A recipient who cannot be messaged (closed inbox, system/notification account, or a 1:1 block) returns HTTP 403 with type https://api.x.com/2/problems/recipient-not-messageable.
